What is left: This kills the route boone-higman-via-stabilizer-engines. A finitely presented stabilizer engine requires its simple envelope S to be finitely presented already, and a finitely presented simple envelope is Boone–Higman for the input. So the route is circular. Its last hole is false, with an explicit counterexample, Z V_Z.

The obstruction also covers a whole class of hosts: those in which the input, or its simple envelope, is the full isotropy of a free factor inside a finitely presented, locally moving full group. They all fail at the same step, the finite-support lemma for the germ cocycle.

It also shows which hosts could escape. They must break the finite support of the cocycle, for exam

Converse germ lemma: let H be torsion-free abelian and F_2[H] -> S(G) an injective monomial representation, where G is an ample Hausdorff groupoid. Then some point has pairwise distinct germs. Consequence: no group containing Z^(r+2) embeds monomially in LC(X) ⋊ (Z^r x F_d), even up to conjugacy or matrix amplification, for any compact Q-space X and any d. The bound is sharp at Z^(r+1). So the full-group route to (E) dies at the decidable groups Z^4, SL_4(Z) and Thompson's F, T and V."]. What is left: This kills a whole class of approaches to the last-missing hole (E) of the route cantor-crossed-hosts-via-boundary-products-of-z2-sft-hosts, at bounty 37. Every monomial (full-group or germ-lemma) embedding dies once G contains Z^4, for every Omega, every d and every compact space X.
- Invariant: the ball separation of the germ orbit.
- Where every member dies: at the tree-centroid slab, whose O(k^2) points must cut the cube [k]^4, and that needs Theta(k^3).

The earlier Kazhdan-orbit results were group-level only and left an algebra loophole. The converse germ lemma closes that loophole for abelian inputs, so this kill holds at algebra level.
